chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Meat is the chief of foods in the world and the Hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the status of meat in Islam?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish the superior status of meat (*lawn*) as the pinnacle of sustenance, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that physical nourishment directly supports spiritual vitality. This narration underscores the holistic Islamic perspective where bodily health is not merely worldly but intrinsically linked to one's standing in the Hereafter, validating the consumption of halal meat as a blessed act.
